user_paid_keys_logging.detail: routes/route.ts destructures user_paid_keys into a local var, passes it to the router for in-memory provider calls, then sets req.body.user_paid_keys='[REDACTED]' (line 231) so any downstream/error logger sees the redaction. The outer catch emits only error.message (no req.body). No logger (anfis_routing_logs, logLlmCall, tool-call-logger) receives user_paid_keys. BYOK custody (encrypted at-rest storage) is future/inert (BYOK_CUSTODY_ENABLED default OFF). Matches the privacy posture. CAVEAT: the PROMPT is logged in previews (prompt_preview 200, request_text 500) for routing analytics — disclosed, and separate from key handling.

free_tier_gate_ip_spoofing.source_pattern: gateIp = (x-forwarded-for).split(',')[0]  — a classically spoofable pattern; meterRun keys anonymous callers by i:${ip}, ANON_RUNS_PER_DAY default 5.
free_tier_gate_ip_spoofing.interpretation: The three responses form ONE monotonic counter (4,3,2 by processing order) across TWO different spoofed IPs. A working spoof would have reset the .22 request to remaining=4; it continued to 2 instead. So the handler is NOT keying on the client-supplied X-Forwarded-For — Railway's edge normalizes XFF so split(',')[0] is the real client IP. The gate is NOT bypassable via X-Forwarded-For on this deployment.
free_tier_gate_ip_spoofing.hardening_note_LOW_informational: Correctness depends on the edge proxy normalizing XFF. If the deployment ever moves behind a proxy that APPENDS (preserving a client-supplied leftmost), the gate becomes bypassable. Recommend deriving the client IP from Express req.ip with an explicit `trust proxy` hop count, rather than raw x-forwarded-for[0], so the gate does not depend on edge behavior.

agent_id_impersonation.detail: F2 fix (2026-06-01): an agent-scoped key must match its bound agent (403 on mismatch); a shared REPID_API_KEYS env key may NOT target a specific agent_id (403). llm_complete scope required for agent-scoped keys (403 if missing).

prompt_injection_into_HAL.detail: /complete routes the prompt to an LLM provider (standard proxy). HAL scoring is a SEPARATE call (/score-event), covered by REPID-ENG-001/003. No privileged HAL decision is made inside /complete from the prompt.
